_palette: Colour scheme, from palettes/. One of the brand palettes: cyber-orange, strata-yellow, prisma-blue. Override per build with --palette. Setting it here also overrides a style that pins its own palette, which nyan does -- leave it out of a customer file unless that is what you want.
_logoSvg: Placeholder mark. Replace with the customer's logo as INLINE SVG, optimised to <= 2 KB. A traced-path export can be 40 KB and will silently break the page. Keep viewBox 0 0 24 24 and use currentColor so it inherits the theme accent.
logoSvg: <svg viewBox="0 0 24 24" width="22" height="22" aria-hidden="true" fill="none" stroke="currentColor" stroke-width="1.9" stroke-linecap="round" stroke-linejoin="round"><path d="M4 7.5 12 3l8 4.5v5.2c0 4.6-3.3 8.5-8 9.3-4.7-.8-8-4.7-8-9.3Z"/><path d="M12 8.2v4.4"/><path d="M12 15.6h.01"/></svg>
_portalName: Heading under the portal logo. Rendered into the #heading markup by the shell, NOT via gp_portal_name -- PAN-OS applies that variable with .html(), which would replace the login/download switch spans and leave the download page reading 'Sign in'. Names the service, not the company: this same string is a small eyebrow on the login and download pages but the whole <h1> on logout, and a value carrying {{COMPANY}} wraps that heading to two lines as soon as the company name is long. The company is already on every one of these pages -- it is the wordmark beside the logo.
_portalLogoSvg: The GlobalProtect portal MARK, as SVG source -- the symbol only, no company name. The name is rendered as text beside it, from `company`, so it follows a rename and takes its colour from the page. Do not draw it in here: an SVG cannot measure text, the viewBox is fixed, and a name longer than the artwork would simply be clipped. Separate from logoSvg because the portal needs this as a percent-encoded data: URI rather than inline markup -- the build does that encoding, so write plain SVG here, with single quotes for attributes. Colour it with the S_* tokens, never a literal hex and never currentColor: this artwork is an isolated document and inherits nothing from the page. The build renders it TWICE, binding S_* to the palette's light values for one copy and its d_ values for the other, and the shells switch between the two in CSS. Keep it square -- it is drawn into a square box.
portalLogoSvg: <svg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 32 32'><rect width='32' height='32' rx='9' fill='{{S_ACCENT}}'/><g transform='translate(16,16) scale(.85) translate(-12,-12.5)'><path d='M4 7.5 12 3l8 4.5v5.2c0 4.6-3.3 8.5-8 9.3-4.7-.8-8-4.7-8-9.3Z' fill='{{S_ACCENT_INK}}'/></g></svg>
_portalLogoSvgDark: Optional. Set it only when the dark-scheme mark is different ARTWORK -- a different symbol, a knockout treatment -- rather than the same drawing in different colours. Left out, the dark copy is portalLogoSvg with S_* bound to the palette's dark values, which is what a mark built from the tokens wants.
_logoutMessages: The seven GlobalProtect logout messages. PAN-OS selects one by index via logout.esp?code=N, so all seven must be present and in order. This array is the only supported way to change logout wording. Entries 3, 4 and 5 are admin-only errors an end user cannot act on, so they name a real contact instead of saying 'contact system administrator' -- {{CONTACT_NAME}} resolves to the support address, or to the words 'IT support' when supportUrl is set.
logoutMessages: You have successfully logged out of GlobalProtect portal.
The GlobalProtect portal is not licensed. Purchase or activate the license for your GlobalProtect subscription.
User not authenticated to GlobalProtect portal.
System error, failed to delete user session. Contact {{CONTACT_NAME}}.
Cannot create user session, maximum capacity reached. Contact {{CONTACT_NAME}}.
Your login session has expired and you have been logged out for security reasons. Please log in again if you wish to continue.

_defaultGloss: Shown when the blocked category is not in the map below. Must be true for every category, so keep it general.
defaultGloss: This category is restricted by company policy.
_continueGrantText: How long a Continue/Override grant lasts. PAN-OS defaults to 15 minutes but this is administrator-configurable per firewall, so it must match your actual URL Admin Override timeout rather than being hardcoded in the page.
_redirect: OPT-IN. When a blocked category has a company-sanctioned equivalent, the URL block page can name it and hand the user over after a countdown. Off unless `enabled` is true AND `categories` below maps at least one category -- with both unset, not one byte of this reaches a page. It applies to the URL block page ONLY: no other response page has a <category/> token to key on, and the two coach pages already carry a Continue action a countdown would race.

redirect._enabled: The toggle. Leave false until the sanctioned apps below are ALLOWED by policy -- see the warning on `categories`.
redirect._seconds: Default countdown, 1-60. Override per category. Long enough to read one sentence and cancel; 10 is deliberately slower than it needs to be for someone who was expecting the site.
redirect._message: Default notice text. `{app}` is replaced with that category's `app`. Override per category for a service that needs a different sentence.
redirect.message: Taking you to {app} — the approved alternative for this.
redirect._categories: category -> the sanctioned app to forward to. WARNING: the target must be permitted by the security policy that produced the block, or the user is sent to a page that blocks them. The page will not loop on that -- served as the blocked site, it can see it is being blocked ON a sanctioned app and refuses to hop again, so a wrong entry here costs one wasted redirect rather than a trap -- but only policy can make the target reachable. Each category must also appear in `categories` above with tone `calm`; the build refuses a redirect on a warn or critical category, because a user must never be forwarded off a security block. `url` must be an absolute https:// URL: it is read from this file and never from <url/>, which is chosen by whoever the user was trying to reach. Optional per entry: `seconds` and `message`. Example: "online-storage-and-backup": { "app": "Company Drive", "url": "https://drive.example.com/", "seconds": 5, "message": "Work files belong on {app}. Taking you there." }

_categories: PAN-OS exposes no severity or reason variable and serves one page per type, so this map is applied client-side by reading the substituted <category/> value. Tone is one of calm | warn | critical. Covers the categories responsible for nearly all real blocks -- everything else falls back to defaultGloss.

command-and-control.gloss: Sites in this category are used to remote-control computers that are already infected.

malware.gloss: This site is known to distribute software that can steal data or take over your device.

phishing.gloss: This site is impersonating a real sign-in page to collect passwords.

ransomware.gloss: This site is linked to ransomware, which encrypts files and demands payment.

grayware.gloss: This site hosts unwanted software — not clearly malicious, but not safe to run on a work device.

newly-registered-domain.gloss: This domain was registered very recently. New domains are blocked for a short period because they are frequently used in scams.

parked.gloss: This domain has no real content. Parked domains are often placeholders for scams or malware.

dynamic-dns.gloss: This address uses a dynamic DNS service, commonly used to hide where a site is actually hosted.

unknown.gloss: This site has not been categorised yet, so it is blocked as a precaution.

insufficient-content.gloss: There is not enough content on this site to classify it, so it is blocked as a precaution.

hacking.gloss: This site distributes tools or instructions for attacking computer systems.

proxy-avoidance-and-anonymizers.gloss: This site is designed to bypass network security controls.

shopping.gloss: Shopping sites are not available on the company network.

streaming-media.gloss: Streaming sites are not available on the company network, mainly to protect bandwidth.

games.gloss: Games are not available on the company network.

social-networking.gloss: Social networks are not available on the company network.

web-advertisements.gloss: Advertising and tracking content is blocked across the company network.
